identity.title: Hydrocarbon Emission Rings in Protoplanetary Disks Induced by Dust Evolution

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report observations of resolved C$_2$H emission rings within the gas-rich protoplanetary disks of TW Hya and DM Tau using the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA).

question.value: Why do C2H (and c-C3H2) emission rings appear at the edge of the mm-dust (pebble) disk in TW Hya and DM Tau, and what physical/chemical conditions (UV field, C/O) are needed to produce them?

analysis_steps.goal: Stack lines and derive disk geometry and radial profiles

method.value: Stack lines to make integrated map; derive PA and inclination from outer C2H ring; deproject to radial brightness profile

evidence.quote: For both disks, we derive a disk position angle and inclination from the outer C$_2$H ring, which we use to deproject the image to create a disk brightness profile.

analysis_steps.goal: Exclude dust optical depth as ring origin

method.value: Compare ring locations to dust optical depth from literature models

evidence.loc: 3.3 Dust Optical Depth and Ring Structure
evidence.quote: Thus, the outer ring is not an effect of dust optical depth and is the result of a change in molecular abundance.

method.value: Three-component dust disk models (inner, sub-mm, UV-dominated), uniform C/O tests, then parametrized C and O depletion; compare simulated N=4-3 emission to observations

evidence.quote: The “best-fit” emission images of for both disks are shown in Fig. [9](#fig:best).

software: Monte Carlo radiative transfer (Dullemond et al. 2002)

key_parameters.value: Gas-to-dust mass ratio 100; dust size distribution power law exponent 3.5; cosmic ray rate ~1e-19 s^-1; models sampled at 5 Myr (TW Hya) and 1 Myr (DM Tau)

evidence.quote: Thus we have run our models with a rate that is reduced compared to the interstellar medium by two orders of magnitude ($\sim 10^{-19}$ s$^{-1}$, with an attenuation parameter of 96 g/cm$^2$).

assumptions.value: Same TW Hya UV field used for both systems; 8:2 astrosilicate:graphite

evidence.quote: we use the TW Hya radiation field for both systems

fitting.value: Parameters chosen heuristically, no formal fit

evidence.quote: The parameters are chosen heuristically for each disk to investigate what C and O distribution best reproduce the observed C$_2$H observations.

validation.value: Predicted emission matches observations within a factor of 1.5; test with 10x higher gas mass

evidence.quote: the predicted emission distribution shown in Fig. [9](#fig:best) matches observations within a factor of 1.5.

findings_qualitative.value: C2H rings lie at the edge of the mm-dust disk in both TW Hya and DM Tau; c-C3H2 shares the TW Hya ring

evidence.quote: In each case the emission ring is found to arise at the edge of the observable disk of mm-sized grains (pebbles) traced by (sub)mm-wave continuum emission.

claims.hypothesis: Hydrocarbon rings arise from dust evolution (settling, drift) that raises UV penetration and the C/O ratio
claims.experiment: Thermo-chemical models with dust stratification and varied C/O compared to ALMA C2H maps
claims.result: Stratification alone underpredicts emission; C/O ≳ 1 and UV-dominated outer disk needed, matching within factor 1.5
claims.finding: Grain motions lead to hydrocarbon-rich chemistry in surface layers and outer disk

evidence.quote: reproducing the emission from C$_2$H requires a strong UV field and C/O $> 1$ in the upper disk atmosphere and outer disk

claims.hypothesis: High dust optical depth explains the ring/hole structure
claims.experiment: Compare ring positions with literature optical depth
claims.result: Outer rings lie where dust is optically thin
claims.finding: A chemical abundance effect, not optical depth, causes the rings

evidence.loc: 3.3 Dust Optical Depth and Ring Structure
evidence.quote: Thus high dust optical depth is not enough to explain the inner hole and a chemical effect is needed

claims.hypothesis: Photodissociation of carbonaceous grains could supply C2H
claims.experiment: Equilibrium abundance estimate and time-dependent model
claims.result: Equilibrium abundance ~5e-10 vs ~1e-7 needed unless oxygen is depleted
claims.finding: Carbon extraction from CO with O depletion is more likely

evidence.loc: 5.4 Photodissociation of Carbonaceous Grains as the Origin of Simple Hydrocarbons
evidence.quote: the equilibrium abundance of C$_2$H would be $\sim 5 \times 10^{-10}$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: High dust optical depth rejected as sole cause of ring; photodissociation of a-C:H/PAH as carbon source disfavored

evidence.loc: 3.3 Dust Optical Depth and Ring Structure
